title: SQL Injection - Admin Login Bypass
impact: Allows an attacker to bypass authentication and log in as any user, including the administrator, without knowing the password, leading to full account takeover.
remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements instead of string concatenation when building SQL queries; never trust raw user input in a query.

title: SQL Injection - UNION-Based User Data Extraction via Search
payload_used: ')) UNION SELECT id, email, password, '4','5','6','7','8','9' FROM Users--
impact: Allows an attacker to extract arbitrary data from other database tables through a product search endpoint, including user emails and password hashes, enabling credential cracking and further account compromise.
remediation: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements for all search inputs, validate and sanitize input types, and apply least-privilege database permissions so the search query's DB account cannot read unrelated tables like Users.

title: Reflected XSS via Search Query
impact: An attacker can craft a malicious link containing the payload and trick a victim into clicking it, causing arbitrary JavaScript to execute in the victim's browser session, potentially leading to session hijacking, credential theft, or phishing.
remediation: Encode/escape all user-supplied input before rendering it in HTML output, implement a strict Content Security Policy (CSP), and use frameworks that auto-escape output by default (e.g. Angular/React's built-in sanitization).

title: Stored XSS via Customer Feedback
impact: The payload is persisted in the backend and executes every time any user (including admins) views the page displaying it, enabling session hijacking, credential theft, or defacement against every visitor without needing to resend the payload.
remediation: Sanitize and encode user-generated content on output (and ideally on input too), store feedback as plain text rather than rendered HTML, and enforce a strict Content Security Policy to block inline/javascript: execution.
